surveys.territory: Territory H: explicit and computer-assisted results — RH verification height records, explicit prime-counting inequalities (psi, theta, pi), explicit zero-free regions and zero-density estimates feeding them, Turing-method/argument bounds, explicit critical-line subconvexity, Mertens-function bounds, partial-RH transfer theorems, and Skewes-region computations. State of the art as of August 2026.

entries.result: RH verification height record
entries.statement: All 12,363,153,437,138 nontrivial zeros beta+i*gamma of zeta with 0 < gamma <= 3,000,175,332,800 (i.e. height 3*10^12) have beta = 1/2, verified rigorously with interval arithmetic (isolated via Turing's method). This independently confirms and exceeds by 22% the non-rigorous Gourdon-Demichel 10^13-zeros computation's rigorous predecessors (Wedeniwski, Franke et al.).
entries.authors: David J. Platt, Timothy S. Trudgian
entries.technique: Rigorous Riemann-Siegel/Booker-Platt band-limited zeta evaluation with interval arithmetic, Gram-point bracketing, Turing's method for completeness
entries.bottleneck: Pure compute cost scales roughly linearly in T with a t^{1/2}-ish per-evaluation cost; no one has funded/coordinated a rigorous push past 3e12 since 2020. Turing-method constants (now improved by Bellotti-Wong 2024) and per-point evaluation cost are the levers.
entries.gap: Six years old and unextended. Modern Arb + improved Turing constants + cheaper hardware make a rigorous extension (or an independent re-verification of a large-height window) a pure pipeline-optimization problem. Also: no kernel-checked formalization of the Turing criterion exists anywhere.
entries.optimization_variables: Turing-method constants, band-limited interpolation parameters, interval evaluation precision schedule, gram-block partitioning
entries.computational_tractability: Full re-run is supercomputer-scale; windowed spot-verification at any height is laptop-scale with Arb
entries.formalization_tractability: Turing criterion lemma is a plausible medium Lean target; full pipeline is not

entries.result: Classical zero-free region record (March 2026)
entries.statement: zeta(sigma+it) != 0 whenever t >= 3 and sigma >= 1 - 1/(4.896 log t). Improves the Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang 2022/2024 constant 5.558691 by about 12%, adapting Heath-Brown's Linnik-constant machinery.
entries.authors: Chiara Bellotti, Tim Trudgian, Andrew Yang
entries.constant: 1/(4.896 log t) for t >= 3; previous record 1/(5.558691 log t) for |t| >= 2 (MTY, arXiv:2212.06867)
entries.technique: Heath-Brown-style trigonometric-polynomial / smoothed sum machinery made explicit, plus the RH verification height 3e12 for small t
entries.bottleneck: Choice of non-negative trigonometric polynomial and smoothing weights; every explicit prime-counting bound downstream (psi, theta, primes between powers, Mertens) was computed against the OLD 5.558691 constant and has not yet been re-propagated.
entries.gap: Five months old: essentially none of the downstream explicit literature (Fiori-Kadiri-Swidinsky psi bounds, Lee's kth-powers tables of Feb 2026, Lee-Leong Mertens constant) has been recomputed with 4.896. This is an unharvested propagation cascade.
entries.optimization_variables: Trigonometric polynomial coefficients, mollifier/smoothing kernel, split-point between classical and Korobov-Vinogradov regions
entries.computational_tractability: Propagation recomputation is days of mpmath work per downstream paper
entries.formalization_tractability: Hard (needs explicit-formula machinery in Lean); the de-la-Vallee-Poussin shape with a worse constant might be a feasible long-term Lean target

entries.result: Korobov-Vinogradov explicit zero-free region
entries.statement: zeta has no zeros for sigma >= 1 - 1/(48.0718 (log|t|)^{2/3} (log log|t|)^{1/3}) asymptotically (Bellotti 2024, improving MTY's 55.241 and their asymptotic 48.1588); MTY 2022: no zeros for sigma >= 1 - 1/(55.241 (log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3}), |t| >= 3.
entries.authors: Chiara Bellotti; Michael J. Mossinghoff, Timothy S. Trudgian, Andrew Yang
entries.citation: Bellotti, 'Explicit bounds for the Riemann zeta function and a new zero-free region', J. Math. Anal. Appl. (2024), S0022247X24001719; MTY arXiv:2212.06867, Res. Number Theory (2024)
entries.technique: Explicit Vinogradov integral / exponential-sum bounds (Ford-style) with careful explicit constants in the van der Corput ranges
entries.bottleneck: Explicit exponential-sum constants are far from Ford's asymptotic quality in the transition range exp(64) <= t <= exp(1000); the crossover ordinate where KV beats classical is astronomically large.
entries.gap: The explicit KV region only bites for |t| > e^481958 in Bellotti's version; shrinking the ordinate where KV-type beats classical-type is wide open and is mostly a finite optimization over exponent-pair/van der Corput parameters.
entries.optimization_variables: Exponent pairs, Vinogradov mean-value parameter choices, range-splitting ordinates
entries.verified_via: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X24001719 (located via search; constants cross-checked against search summaries)
entries.computational_tractability: Parameter re-optimization is symbolic+numeric, laptop-scale
entries.formalization_tractability: Very hard

entries.result: Sharpest unconditional psi(x) error bounds
entries.statement: For all x > 2: |psi(x) - x| < 9.22106 * x * (log x)^{3/2} * exp(-0.8476836 sqrt(log x)); and for log x >= 3000: |psi(x) - x| < 4.47e-15 * x. Refines Pintz's method as applied by Platt-Trudgian, splitting zeros into extra regions with heavy computation.
entries.authors: Andrew Fiori, Habiba Kadiri, Joshua Swidinsky
entries.constant: 9.22106, exponent constant 0.8476836; asymptotic-regime constant 4.47e-15 for log x >= 3000
entries.technique: Pintz-style zero-splitting: contributions partitioned by zero height and distance from the 1-line, each region estimated with the best available zero-free region + zero density + verified zeros to 3e12
entries.bottleneck: Inputs frozen at 2022 values: MTY 5.558691 classical region, KLN zero density, 3e12 verification height. Every input has since improved (BTY 4.896, Bellotti log-free density 2025, explicit Ingham 2025).
entries.gap: A straight re-run of the FKS optimization with the 2025-2026 inputs (4.896 zero-free region, Bellotti log-free zero density, Bellotti-Wong N(T)) should mechanically improve both constants; nobody has published it as of Aug 2026.
entries.optimization_variables: Zero-region partition boundaries, per-region estimate choices, the smoothing parameter in Pintz's method, verification-height/zero-density trade-off
entries.verified_via: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02588 (constants from search-result summary of abstract)
entries.computational_tractability: High: this is exactly a numerical-optimization pipeline; the authors published code/tables
entries.formalization_tractability: The final inequality (with worse constants) is a conceivable Lean target via a verified finite computation, but the analytic inputs are hard

entries.result: PNT error terms for pi(x), theta(x), psi(x) (Johnston-Yang)
entries.statement: For all x >= 2: |psi(x) - x| <= 9.39 * x * (log x)^{1.515} * exp(-0.8274 sqrt(log x)), with analogous explicit bounds for |theta(x)-x| and |pi(x)-li(x)|; best known for large x in its era, relying on explicit zero-free regions and zero-density estimates.
entries.authors: Daniel R. Johnston, Andrew Yang
entries.technique: Combines Pintz zero-splitting with explicit zero-density (KLN) and the 3e12 verification, optimizing the interplay
entries.bottleneck: Same frozen 2022 inputs as FKS; also the (log x)^{1.515} power is an artifact of the density-estimate shape, itself improvable via Bellotti's log-free density
entries.gap: Re-optimization against 2025-2026 inputs unpublished; additionally the medium-x range (x between ~e^60 and e^3000) is governed by crude region-splitting that authors acknowledge is lossy
entries.optimization_variables: Region split points, density-estimate selection per region, smoothing kernel
entries.computational_tractability: High
entries.formalization_tractability: Low-medium

entries.result: All-range explicit theta(x) bounds
entries.statement: Explicit bounds |theta(x) - x| <= eps * x (tabulated eps by range) and |theta(x)-x| <= c_k * x/(log x)^k for k = 1..5 with full tables of c_k over all x-ranges; the standard reference tables used by essentially every explicit application since 2021.
entries.authors: Samuel Broadbent, Habiba Kadiri, Allysa Lumley, Nathan Ng, Kirsten Wilk
entries.constant: Tabulated (e.g. c_1-type constants by range; exact values in ancillary tables, not a single closed form)
entries.technique: Explicit formula with verified zeros to 3e12 + zero-free regions + smoothing, optimized per range
entries.bottleneck: Tables computed against 2020-era inputs; each improvement in zero-free region or verification height stales them
entries.gap: A regenerated table set using BTY 4.896 and Bellotti densities would improve many entries; also the tables are exactly the kind of enclosure-checked-computation artifact that Arb enclosures could carry end-to-end (currently they are careful floats)
entries.optimization_variables: Smoothing function per range, range endpoints, k-dependent trade-offs
entries.computational_tractability: High; regeneration is a well-scoped compute job
entries.formalization_tractability: Individual table entries could be Lean-enclosure-checked via interval computation

entries.result: Explicit zero-counting / argument bound (Turing-method backbone)
entries.statement: |N(T) - (T/(2*pi)) log(T/(2*pi*e))| <= 0.10076 log T + 0.24460 log log T + 8.08344 for all T >= e. Improves Hasanalizade-Shen-Wong; main gain from new subconvexity bounds for zeta(sigma_k + it) on interior lines.
entries.authors: Chiara Bellotti, Peng-Jie Wong (appendix by Andrew Fiori)
entries.technique: Backlund/Rosser argument-bound method with optimized convexity interpolation between explicit sigma-line bounds
entries.bottleneck: The sigma_k-line subconvexity constants; the Feb 2026 Revers improvement of the critical-line estimate postdates this paper and is not incorporated
entries.gap: Plugging Revers (arXiv:2602.05614) and Patel-Yang sub-Weyl (66.7 t^{27/164}) constants into the Bellotti-Wong optimization is an unharvested mechanical improvement; the leading constant 0.10076 directly tightens Turing's method for all future verification computations
entries.optimization_variables: Choice of sigma_k lines, convexity interpolation weights, subconvexity constants fed in
entries.computational_tractability: High: finite optimization over documented parameters
entries.formalization_tractability: Medium: Backlund's method is one of the more formalizable explicit arguments

entries.result: Explicit critical-line subconvexity records
entries.statement: van der Corput regime: |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 0.618 t^{1/6} log t class bounds (Hiary-Patel-Yang 2022/2024, correcting the flawed Kusmin-Landau constant used by earlier records), newly improved by Revers (Feb 2026) via a refined explicit van der Corput method plus computation. Sub-Weyl regime: |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 66.7 t^{27/164} for t >= 3, sharpest known for t >= exp(61) (Patel-Yang 2023). Note 27/164 = 0.16463... < 1/6.
entries.authors: Ghaith A. Hiary, Dhir Patel, Andrew Yang; Michael Revers
entries.constant: 66.7 t^{27/164} (t >= 3, best for t >= e^61); HPY t^{1/6}-class constant improved again Feb 2026 (exact new constant in 2602.05614 full text)
entries.technique: Explicit van der Corput second/third derivative tests with corrected Kusmin-Landau lemma; explicit Bombieri-Iwaniec-style machinery for sub-Weyl
entries.bottleneck: Explicit exponent-pair constants; the crossover height e^61 where sub-Weyl wins is huge because the 66.7 prefactor is crude
entries.gap: Lowering the sub-Weyl prefactor 66.7 (or the crossover e^61) is an explicit finite optimization; these bounds feed Bellotti-Wong N(T) and all zero-free regions, so gains cascade
entries.optimization_variables: Exponent pairs, Farey-dissection parameters, prefactor vs range trade-offs
entries.computational_tractability: High for constant-tuning; the lab can also numerically map actual max|zeta| vs bound to locate slack
entries.formalization_tractability: van der Corput lemmas are self-contained enough to be a realistic Lean project

entries.result: Partial-RH transfer theorems (verification height to conditional bounds)
entries.statement: Büthe: Schoenfeld's RH-conditional bounds, e.g. |pi(x) - li(x)| <= sqrt(x) log(x)/(8*pi) for 2657 < x, hold unconditionally whenever 4.92 sqrt(x/log x) <= T0, where T0 is a height of verified RH. Johnston: condition weakened to (9.06/log log x) sqrt(x/log x) <= T0, extending the Schoenfeld-bound range to roughly x <= 1.101 * 10^26 given T0 = 3e12.
entries.authors: Jan Büthe; Daniel R. Johnston
entries.technique: Weil-Barner explicit formula with Logan's extremal band-limited test functions; Johnston adds an iterative bootstrap
entries.bottleneck: The test-function choice: Logan functions are extremal for one specific tail criterion, not for the actual composite objective; the constant 4.92/9.06 encodes that mismatch
entries.gap: The kernel is an explicit optimization surface that has been touched exactly twice (Büthe 2016, Johnston 2021); a numerically optimized kernel (linear programming over band-limited functions, as in bounded-gap-prime and sphere-packing work) plausibly lowers the constant and extends the unconditional Schoenfeld range beyond 10^26 with zero new zero computations
entries.optimization_variables: Band-limited test function (infinite-dimensional, discretizable), truncation height, iteration schedule
entries.computational_tractability: Very high: the lab's weil.py explicit-formula and test-function machinery is exactly this
entries.formalization_tractability: Medium-low

entries.result: Explicit Mertens function bounds
entries.statement: M(x) <= x * exp(-0.209 (log x)^{3/5} (log log x)^{-1/5}) for x >= 3 (first explicit bound of Korobov-Vinogradov shape), plus explicit M(x) << x exp(-eta_1 sqrt(log x)) versions; computationally, |M(x)|/sqrt(x) verified < 0.571 for x <= 10^16 (Hurst).
entries.authors: Ethan S. Lee (and Leong for the 0.209 refinement); Greg Hurst (computation)
entries.constant: 0.209 in the (log x)^{3/5}(log log x)^{-1/5} exponent; Hurst: M(x) computed exactly to x = 10^16
entries.technique: Comparison of M(x) with a short sum over zeta zeros, using explicit bounds for 1/zeta and the verified-zeros database
entries.bottleneck: Explicit 1/zeta(s) bounds near the 1-line and the zero-free region constant (derived from the now-superseded KV constants)
entries.gap: 0.209 was computed before BTY 4.896 and before Bellotti's 2025 log-free density; re-propagation should improve it. Hurst's 10^16 computation is 8 years old and a modern segmented-sieve + Helfgott-Thompson mu-computation could push the exact-computation frontier and the 0.571 empirical constant
entries.optimization_variables: Truncation height of the zero sum, 1/zeta bound selection, sieve computation range
entries.computational_tractability: High on both analytic-propagation and computational sides
entries.formalization_tractability: The lab already has a kernel-checked Mertens theorem; the explicit M(x) bound is a distinct, harder target

entries.result: Primes between consecutive kth powers
entries.statement: There is a prime between n^155 and (n+1)^155 for all n >= 1 (Cully-Hugill, via a new explicit Goldston-type truncated explicit-formula error). Primes between consecutive cubes for all n >= exp(exp(32.537)). Lee (Feb 2026): a prime between consecutive 86th powers for all n >= 1, with tables covering k >= 65, computed from minimal Littlewood-shape zero-free regions.
entries.authors: Michaela Cully-Hugill; Ethan Simpson Lee
entries.constant: k = 86 (all n), k = 70 (subsequence), cubes threshold exp(exp(32.537))
entries.technique: Truncated Riemann-von Mangoldt explicit formula with explicit Goldston error (arXiv:2402.04272 gives the O(x/T) version), fed by zero-free regions + verification height
entries.bottleneck: Lee's Feb 2026 tables use pre-March-2026 zero-free regions; the BTY 4.896 constant arrived three weeks after his revision. Also the Goldston-error smoothing is a tunable kernel
entries.gap: Recomputing Lee's five tables with 4.896 (and with Bellotti-Wong N(T)) should lower k = 86; the author explicitly solicits improvements. Legendre-conjecture-adjacent record-chasing with fully mechanical inputs
entries.optimization_variables: Zero-free region constant, explicit-formula truncation T, smoothing weight in Goldston error, interval asymmetry
entries.computational_tractability: Very high: table regeneration
entries.formalization_tractability: Low

entries.result: Explicit error for the truncated Riemann-von Mangoldt explicit formula
entries.statement: psi(x) = x - sum_{|gamma|<=T} x^rho/rho + explicit error, with the error made fully explicit with an O(x log^2(xT)/T)-shaped bound and, in the 2024 version, an explicit O(x/T) error term (improving constants for applications to primes between powers).
entries.authors: Michaela Cully-Hugill, Daniel R. Johnston
entries.constant: Explicit constants in the x/T term (tabulated in paper; shape c * x/T for stated ranges)
entries.technique: Goldston's 1983 method made explicit: counting primes in short windows around x paired with zero-density input
entries.bottleneck: The smoothing window and the treatment of the log^2 factor; measured slack between the bound and the true error is unquantified
entries.gap: Nobody has published a numerical map of actual-error/bound ratio across (x, T); large measured slack in a specific regime would pinpoint which lemma to sharpen. The lab's explicit.py computes both sides directly
entries.optimization_variables: Window width h, weight function, zero-density input, T-range case splits
entries.computational_tractability: Very high with existing lab machinery
entries.formalization_tractability: Low-medium

entries.result: Explicit zero-density estimates
entries.statement: KLN 2022: N(sigma,T) <= C1(sigma) T^{8(1-sigma)/3} (log T)^{5-2sigma} + C2(sigma) log^2 T for sigma >= 0.60 (explicit C1, C2 tabulated). Bellotti 2025: first explicit LOG-FREE zero-density estimate (J. Number Theory 269 (2025) 37-77, arXiv:2405.12545), strong enough for a log-free KV zero-free region. Also explicit Ingham-type N(sigma,T) (arXiv:2507.15184, July 2025).
entries.authors: Habiba Kadiri, Allysa Lumley, Nathan Ng; Chiara Bellotti; (Ingham-explicit authors, 2025)
entries.constant: Tabulated C1(sigma), C2(sigma); e.g. KLN improves Ramare's earlier explicit density constants
entries.technique: Mollified second-moment method with explicit mollifier coefficients (KLN); Turan-power-sum/log-free machinery (Bellotti)
entries.bottleneck: Mollifier length and coefficients are chosen for tractability, not optimality; explicit densities remain far above what is known asymptotically (Guth-Maynard 2024 exponent 30/13 has NO explicit version)
entries.gap: An explicit version of even a weakened Guth-Maynard-type estimate would be transformative for every entry above; more modestly, re-optimizing KLN mollifier coefficients numerically for the specific sigma-ranges used by FKS/Johnston-Yang is unmined
entries.optimization_variables: Mollifier coefficients and length, moment-method smoothing, sigma-range case splits
entries.verified_via: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12545 (located via search; KLN and Ingham-explicit located via search listings)
entries.computational_tractability: Medium-high
entries.formalization_tractability: Very low

entries.result: Skewes region: first sign change of pi(x) - li(x)
entries.statement: There exists x in [1.39792136e316, 1.39847567e316] with pi(x) > li(x) (Saouter-Demichel-style localization); Revers (2025, J. Number Theory) improved the error terms in Lehman's classical method and re-examined crossover regions near 10^316. Lower bound: pi(x) < li(x) for all x <= 10^19 (and up to ~1.39e17 exhaustively by computation).
entries.authors: Yannick Saouter, Patrick Demichel; Michael Revers
entries.citation: Saouter-Demichel, Int. J. Number Theory (2010), doi 10.1142/S1793042110003125; Revers, J. Number Theory (2025), arXiv Jan 2025
entries.constant: Crossover interval [1.39792136e316, 1.39847567e316]; verified pi(x) < li(x) up to at least 10^19
entries.technique: Lehman's integral over verified zeros with explicit error terms; high-precision floating-point zero sums
entries.bottleneck: Lehman-method error terms (partially improved by Revers) and the fact that all published crossover computations are careful floats, not enclosure-checked enclosures
entries.gap: No ball-arithmetic-enclosure-checked version of the crossover localization exists; Revers's improved error terms have not been combined with the 3e12 zero database under enclosure arithmetic to give a hardened (in this lab's sense) crossover interval, possibly narrower
entries.optimization_variables: Lehman kernel parameter (alpha, eta), truncation height, number of zeros used, enclosure precision schedule
entries.computational_tractability: High: heatflow/explicit-formula + rigor.py machinery matches this exactly
entries.formalization_tractability: Low

entries.result: de Bruijn-Newman constant enclosure
entries.statement: 0 <= Lambda <= 0.2. Lower bound Lambda >= 0 by Rodgers-Tao (2018, unconditional; RH is equivalent to Lambda = 0). Upper bound Lambda <= 0.22 by Polymath15 (2019), refined to Lambda <= 0.2 (Polymath15 final version / subsequent slight improvement noted April 2020 by Platt-Trudgian).
entries.authors: Brad Rodgers, Terence Tao; Polymath15 (Tao et al.); D. Platt, T. Trudgian
entries.citation: arXiv:1801.05914 (Rodgers-Tao); Polymath15, Res. Math. Sci. (2019) 'Effective approximation of heat flow evolution of the Riemann xi function'
entries.technique: Upper bound: rigorous numerics on H_t zeros (heat-flow evolution) up to a height, plus a zero-repulsion barrier argument; lower bound: pseudospectra/GUE-statistics argument
entries.bottleneck: Upper bound needs rigorous H_t zero tracking to larger heights plus barrier certificates; cost grows steeply with target Lambda
entries.gap: Untouched since 2020. The lab's heatflow.py (H_t, zero tracking, Lambda machinery) plus Arb could attempt Lambda <= 0.15: the Polymath15 write-up documents the exact computation that would be needed; nobody has redone it with modern Arb and the 3e12 database
entries.optimization_variables: Barrier location, t-mesh for zero tracking, Euler-product approximation order, verification height used
entries.computational_tractability: Medium: serious but well-documented compute pipeline, directly matching existing lab code
entries.formalization_tractability: Very low

entries.result: Verified-zeros infrastructure and rigorous evaluation methods
entries.statement: Platt's database of the 1.2e13 verified zeros (to height 3e12) is available via LMFDB; Arb (Johansson) provides rigorous ball-arithmetic zeta/Riemann-Siegel evaluation used by essentially all post-2017 enclosure-checked computations; a 2024 method paper extends rigorous verification methodology to GRH for other L-functions (arXiv:2408.00187).
entries.authors: David Platt; Fredrik Johansson; (GRH-method authors 2024)
entries.citation: arXiv:2408.00187; Johansson, 'Arb: efficient arbitrary-precision midpoint-radius interval arithmetic', IEEE Trans. Computers (2017)
entries.technique: Band-limited function evaluation, rigorous FFT-based multi-evaluation, Turing/Backlund completeness checks
entries.bottleneck: Per-evaluation cost of rigorous zeta at large height; database access bandwidth for downstream enclosure-checked computations
entries.gap: Most downstream explicit papers still use the database through float summaries rather than end-to-end enclosures; wiring the database into enclosure-carrying recomputations (Skewes, Mertens, psi bounds) is systematically unharvested
entries.optimization_variables: Precision schedules, band-limited interpolation parameters
entries.verified_via: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.00187 (located via search); Arb citation memory-unverified as to exact journal details
entries.computational_tractability: This IS the tooling
entries.formalization_tractability: Lean-side interval arithmetic exists in lab (IntervalExp etc.); bridging to zeta evaluation is the open engineering problem

candidate_projects.title: Propagate the March-2026 zero-free region (4.896) through Lee's kth-powers tables
candidate_projects.description: Lee's Feb 2026 paper (arXiv:2602.14340, k=86 for primes between consecutive kth powers) was finalized three weeks before Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang published the classical zero-free region 1/(4.896 log t) (arXiv:2603.21490), improving on 5.558691. Reimplement Lee's five tables (the Littlewood-form minimal zero-free-region computation plus the explicit-formula inequality) in mpmath, validate against his published k=86/k=70/k>=65 values, then substitute 4.896 and the Bellotti-Wong N(T) bound (0.10076 log T). Falsifiable claim: k drops below 86 for all n. First signal: reproduction of one row of Lee's Table within 24h; the improved k within days. Cheap falsification: if the binding constraint in Lee's optimization is the verification height 3e12 rather than the zero-free constant, the improvement is nil and that is visible from the reproduced table's sensitivity column immediately.
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 1-3 days

candidate_projects.title: Numerically optimized test function for the Buthe-Johnston partial-RH transfer
candidate_projects.description: Johnston's condition (9.06/log log x) sqrt(x/log x) <= T0 for Schoenfeld-type bounds uses Logan's extremal band-limited functions, which are extremal for a tail criterion, not the actual composite objective in the Weil-Barner explicit formula. Discretize the space of band-limited even test functions (say 50-200 coefficients against a Fourier basis with support constraint), and solve the resulting linear/semidefinite program minimizing the constant in Johnston's Theorem 1.4 shape, evaluating both sides with the lab's weil.py explicit-formula machinery against the real zero database. Falsifiable claim: a kernel achieving constant < 9.06 (equivalently, extending the unconditional Schoenfeld range past 1.101e26 with T0=3e12 fixed). First signal: reproduce Johnston's 9.06 from his stated kernel, then show the LP finds any admissible kernel beating it on a coarse grid. Falsified cheaply if the LP optimum equals the Logan value to 3 digits (meaning Logan is near-extremal for the composite objective too).
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 3-7 days

candidate_projects.title: Feed Revers's Feb-2026 critical-line bound into the Bellotti-Wong N(T) optimization
candidate_projects.description: Bellotti-Wong (arXiv:2412.15470) obtain |N(T) - (T/2pi)log(T/2pi e)| <= 0.10076 log T + ... explicitly from subconvexity bounds on sigma_k-lines; their improvement over Hasanalizade-Shen-Wong came precisely from better subconvexity inputs. Revers (arXiv:2602.05614, Feb 2026) improved the explicit van der Corput critical-line estimate after their v2. Extract Bellotti-Wong's optimization (choice of sigma_k lines + convexity interpolation, documented in their appendix), reimplement in mpmath, verify 0.10076, then substitute Revers's constants and re-optimize the sigma_k placement. Any improvement tightens Turing's method globally. First signal: reproduction of 0.10076 within days. Falsified cheaply if the binding term in their optimization is the 1-line or 0-line bound rather than the critical-line one (readable off the reproduced optimization's active constraints).
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 3-7 days

candidate_projects.title: Enclosure-enclosure-checked Skewes crossover via Lehman's method with Revers's error terms
candidate_projects.description: Every published localization of the first pi(x) > li(x) crossover (Saouter-Demichel interval [1.39792136e316, 1.39847567e316]; Revers 2025 improved Lehman error terms) rests on high-precision floating-point sums over zeta zeros. No ball-arithmetic-enclosure-checked version exists. Implement Lehman's integral with the lab's rigor.py (Arb backend) over the first ~2e7 zeros (obtainable from LMFDB/Odlyzko tables via moments.py's ingestion path), carrying Revers's explicit error terms as interval quantities. Deliverable: a hardened (enclosure-carrying) proof that pi(x) > li(x) somewhere in an explicit interval near 1.398e316, possibly narrower than Saouter-Demichel. First signal: enclosure of the Lehman integral at one test point agreeing with published float values, ~1 week. Falsified/blocked cheaply if the required zero precision exceeds the available table precision (checkable on day one by interval-width propagation analysis).
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 1-2 weeks
candidate_projects.key_reference: Saouter-Demichel IJNT 2010, doi 10.1142/S1793042110003125; Revers J. Number Theory 2025

candidate_projects.title: Measure the slack in the explicit truncated Riemann-von Mangoldt error (Cully-Hugill-Johnston)
candidate_projects.description: The explicit O(x/T) error in arXiv:2402.04272 underlies the kth-powers and short-interval records, but the ratio (actual error)/(bound) has never been mapped. The lab's explicit.py computes psi(x) and the truncated zero-sum directly. Compute the true truncation error on a log-spaced grid x in [1e4, 1e12], T in [1e2, 3e6] using the enclosure-checked zero list, and compare to the CHJ bound with their exact constants. Deliverable: a slack map; slack persistently > 5 in the regime that binds Lee's k=86 computation identifies the specific lemma (the Goldston window estimate vs the log^2 term) worth sharpening, and gives a concrete conjectural improved constant to then prove. First signal: slack values on a 10x10 grid in ~2 days. Falsified if slack is < 2 uniformly (bound is near-tight, no room).
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 2-3 days

candidate_projects.title: Re-run the Fiori-Kadiri-Swidinsky psi(x) pipeline with 2025-2026 inputs
candidate_projects.description: FKS's |psi(x)-x| < 9.22106 x (log x)^{3/2} exp(-0.8476836 sqrt(log x)) is an optimization pipeline whose inputs are all superseded: MTY 5.558691 -> BTY 4.896 (classical), MTY 55.241/48.1588 -> Bellotti 48.0718 (KV), KLN density -> Bellotti log-free (2025) + explicit Ingham (2507.15184), HSW N(T) -> Bellotti-Wong 0.10076. Reimplement the Pintz zero-region-splitting optimization (the paper documents the regions and per-region estimates; ancillary code exists) and re-derive both headline constants. Expected outcome: 0.8476836 rises (better exponent constant) and/or 9.22106 and the 4.47e-15 plateau drop. First signal: reproduction of the published constants from published inputs, ~1 week; the update run is then mechanical. Falsified cheaply if reproduction shows the dominant loss is the density estimate in a range where Bellotti's log-free version is weaker than KLN (checkable per-region). Larger effort than the Lee-table project but higher payoff: these are THE reference psi bounds.
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 1-2 weeks

candidate_projects.title: Kernel-checked Turing/Backlund zero-counting criterion in Lean 4
candidate_projects.description: No proof assistant has a verified statement of the Turing-method completeness criterion (if Z(t) has M sign changes in [0,T] and the Backlund/argument bound holds, then N(T) = M), even though every RH verification since 1953 rests on it. Target: formalize in the lab's ZetaLean the elementary implication [explicit S(T) bound] + [sign-change count] => [exact N(T)], with the Bellotti-Wong constants as hypotheses (not proved), and instantiate it kernel-checked for a small window using the existing IntervalExp/Rigor layers to certify sign changes of Z on [0,100], yielding a kernel-checked N(100) = 29. First signal: the criterion statement compiling with sorry-free elementary parts within 1-2 weeks; the numeric instantiation rides existing lab interval machinery. Falsified/blocked if Mathlib's argument-principle support is too weak for even the hypothesis-carrying version (discoverable in days by scoping against Mathlib's ZetaFunction and argument-principle files).
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 1-2 weeks (scoping verdict); 4-8 weeks (instance)
candidate_projects.key_reference: arXiv:2412.15470; Turing (1953); lab lean/ZetaLean Rigor layers

candidate_projects.title: Recompute the explicit Mertens constant 0.209 with the new zero-free cascade
candidate_projects.description: Lee(-Leong)'s M(x) <= x exp(-0.209 (log x)^{3/5} (log log x)^{-1/5}) (arXiv:2208.06141) derives its exponent constant from pre-2025 KV zero-free constants and explicit 1/zeta bounds. The dependence chain (KV constant c -> eta_2 ~ f(c)) is stated explicitly in the paper. Recompute eta_2 with Bellotti 48.0718 and check whether the March-2026 classical region shifts the binding range. Secondary computational arm: extend Hurst's exact M(x) computation beyond 10^16 using Helfgott-Thompson mu-sieving to update the empirical |M(x)|/sqrt(x) < 0.571 record. The lab's criteria.py (Mertens/Mobius face) provides the checking harness, and the lab already holds a kernel-checked Mertens theorem to anchor the Lean-adjacent write-up. First signal: the recomputed eta_2 from the paper's own dependence formula, 2-4 days. Falsified if eta_2 is insensitive to c in the relevant range (visible from the formula immediately).
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 2-4 days

surveys.territory: Territory G: geometry of the Riemann xi function — de Bruijn-Newman flow, Jensen polynomial hyperbolicity, Laguerre-Polya class, higher-order Turan inequalities, zeros of xi^(n), Polya-type universality under differentiation, heat-flow zero dynamics

entries.result: Newman's conjecture: de Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative
entries.statement: Let H_t(z) = integral of e^{tu^2} Phi(u) cos(zu) du with H_0 = (1/8) Xi(z/2). There exists Lambda (de Bruijn-Newman constant) such that H_t has all real zeros iff t >= Lambda; RH is equivalent to Lambda <= 0. Theorem (Rodgers-Tao): Lambda >= 0. Hence RH, if true, is equivalent to Lambda = 0.
entries.constant: Lambda >= 0 (exactly; previous best lower bound was Lambda > -1.15e-11, Saouter-Gourdon-Demichel 2011)
entries.authors: Brad Rodgers, Terence Tao
entries.citation: arXiv:1801.05914; Forum of Mathematics, Pi 8 (2020) e6
entries.technique: Contradiction from Lambda < 0: backward heat-flow dynamics of zeros (Csordas-Smith-Varga ODE system) forces zeros of H_0 into an over-rigid locally-equidistributed configuration incompatible with Montgomery pair-correlation-type estimates for zeta zeros.
entries.bottleneck: The result is sharp in the only improvable direction (Lambda > 0 would disprove RH), so the frontier moved to the upper bound and to quantitative versions of the relaxation mechanism.
entries.gap: Quantitative relaxation-to-equilibrium rates for the zero dynamics of H_t (t in (0, Lambda_upper)) are not pinned down; effective versions of the rigidity dichotomy remain unexplored numerically.
entries.optimization_variables: test functions in the pair-correlation input; time-window and mesoscopic scale parameters in the dynamics argument
entries.computational_tractability: Lab heatflow.py already tracks H_t zeros; the dynamics are directly simulable.
entries.formalization_tractability: Very hard; full argument uses pair correlation machinery far beyond current Mathlib zeta coverage.

entries.result: Polymath15 upper bound for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
entries.statement: Unconditionally Lambda <= 0.22. Conditionally on the numerical verification of RH to height 3x10^12 (Platt-Trudgian, arXiv:2004.09765), the same pipeline yields Lambda <= 0.20 (stated on the Polymath wiki, not formally published). Method: prove H_t is zero-free in an explicit barrier region plus an effective A+B/B_0 approximation showing no zeros above the barrier for t = 0.22.
entries.constant: Lambda <= 0.22 unconditional; Lambda <= 0.2 modulo RH verified to 3x10^12 (wiki-level, unpublished)
entries.authors: D.H.J. Polymath (Polymath15 project, moderated by T. Tao)
entries.citation: arXiv:1904.12438; Research in the Mathematical Sciences 6 (2019)
entries.technique: Effective error bounds for a Riemann-Siegel-type approximation of H_t; interval-arithmetic verification of a zero-free barrier; explicit control of zero motion under the heat flow.
entries.bottleneck: Cost of the barrier computation scales with the RH-verification height; each halving of the bound requires exponentially higher verified height (getting to 0.1 was estimated to need an enormous distributed computation).
entries.gap: The 0.20 improvement enabled by Platt-Trudgian 2020 was never formally written up or pushed further; the public code (github.com/km-git-acc/dbn_upper_bound) has not been rerun with post-2020 heights or with re-optimized barrier placement/mesh.
entries.optimization_variables: barrier location x_0, time t_0, mesh resolution, choice of effective approximant (A+B vs A+B-C), Euler-product tail parameters
entries.computational_tractability: High: public reference code exists; lab has Arb ball arithmetic and heatflow machinery to independently certify the barrier.
entries.formalization_tractability: The effective approximation lemmas are finite and explicit; a Lean port would be a major but well-scoped computation-heavy project.

entries.result: Ki-Kim-Lee: Lambda < 1/2 and finiteness of non-real zeros for t > 0
entries.statement: Lambda < 1/2 (strict improvement of de Bruijn's 1950 bound Lambda <= 1/2). Moreover for every t > 0, H_t has at most finitely many non-real zeros, and all but finitely many zeros of H_t are real and simple.
entries.constant: Lambda < 1/2 (no explicit numerical gap below 1/2 given)
entries.authors: Haseo Ki, Young-One Kim, Jungseob Lee
entries.citation: Advances in Mathematics 222 (2009) 281-306, 'On the de Bruijn-Newman constant'
entries.technique: Saddle point analysis of the integral representation of H_t; classical entire-function theory (Laguerre-Polya class stability under the backward heat operator).
entries.bottleneck: The qualitative 'finitely many non-real zeros' has no effective bound on the count or the height containing them, for given t > 0.
entries.gap: An explicit function N(t) bounding the number (or maximal height) of non-real zeros of H_t for each t in (0, 0.22) has never been extracted; Polymath15 methods make this finitely checkable for specific t.
entries.optimization_variables: saddle-point contour choices; effective constants in the asymptotic expansion of H_t
entries.computational_tractability: Lab can certify absence of non-real zeros of H_t in boxes via enclosures.
entries.formalization_tractability: Moderate-hard; needs Laguerre-Polya theory not in Mathlib.

entries.result: Dobner: Newman's conjecture for the extended Selberg class
entries.statement: Every L-function in the extended Selberg class has an associated de Bruijn-Newman constant Lambda_L, and Lambda_L >= 0 for all of them. The proof avoids all information about zeros of the underlying L-function (unlike Rodgers-Tao, which needs pair-correlation input).
entries.authors: Alexander Dobner
entries.citation: arXiv:2005.05142, 'A New Proof of Newman's Conjecture and a Generalization'
entries.technique: Direct construction: exploits the Euler-product/Dirichlet-series structure to build test points where reality of zeros fails for t < 0, bypassing zero-dynamics entirely.
entries.bottleneck: Method gives non-negativity only; it does not localize where non-real zeros of H_t appear for t < 0, so it contributes nothing to upper bounds.
entries.gap: Quantitative version (how fast do non-real zeros appear as t decreases through 0, for a given L-function) is untouched; comparison of Dobner vs Rodgers-Tao mechanisms on Davenport-Heilbronn-type functions (which are in the extended class and violate RH) is unexplored numerically.
entries.optimization_variables: choice of test points / Dirichlet coefficients exploited in the construction
entries.computational_tractability: High for the Davenport-Heilbronn comparison: lab has epstein.py with Z_dh and the off-line zero.
entries.formalization_tractability: Reported to be much simpler than Rodgers-Tao; plausibly the most formalizable proof of Lambda >= 0.

entries.result: Griffin-Ono-Rolen-Zagier: eventual hyperbolicity of all Jensen polynomials of xi
entries.statement: Let J^{d,n}(X) be the degree-d Jensen polynomial attached to the Taylor coefficients gamma(n) of (-1+4z^2) Lambda(1/2+z) = sum gamma(n) z^{2n}/n! (8 xi normalization). Polya (1927): RH is equivalent to hyperbolicity of J^{d,n} for all d, n >= 0. Theorem: for each fixed d >= 1, J^{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic for all sufficiently large n; moreover suitably renormalized J^{d,n} converge uniformly to the Hermite polynomial H_d(X), and this Hermite universality holds for a large class of sequences (settling the Chen-Jia-Wang conjecture for partitions).
entries.authors: Michael Griffin, Ken Ono, Larry Rolen, Don Zagier
entries.technique: Asymptotics of the derivative sequence gamma(n) (via theta-integral moments) feeding a general Hermite-approximation lemma for Jensen polynomials of admissible sequences.
entries.bottleneck: Fixed-d hyperbolicity for large n is exponentially far from RH (RH needs all d simultaneously; Farmer 2020 argues the d-aspect is the whole difficulty).
entries.gap: Rates: uniformity in d of the Hermite approximation is poor (n >> e^{d/2} in the effective version); closing the d-uniformity gap is the entire remaining problem.
entries.optimization_variables: renormalization sequences A(n), delta(n); admissible-growth class definition; choice of expansion basis (Hermite vs Meixner-Pollaczek per Romik)
entries.computational_tractability: Lab li.py already computes Jensen polynomials and Turan ratios in both normalizations.
entries.formalization_tractability: The Hermite-approximation lemma is elementary asymptotic analysis; a plausible medium-size Lean target.

entries.result: Griffin-Ono-Rolen-Thorner-Tripp-Wagner: effective hyperbolicity, d <= 9.36x10^20
entries.statement: Theorem 1.1: there is c > 0 with J^{d,n}(X) hyperbolic for all d >= 1 and n >= c e^{d/2}. Theorem 1.2: let RH_m(T) assert every zero rho of xi^{(m)}(s) with |Im rho| <= T has Re rho = 1/2; if RH_m(T) holds and d <= floor(T)^2, then J^{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic for all n >= m. Corollary 1.3: since RH_0(3.06x10^10) is known (Platt 2017), J^{d,n} is hyperbolic for all n >= 0 whenever d <= 9.36x10^20.
entries.constant: d <= 9.36x10^20 (all n >= 0); threshold n >= c e^{d/2} with c effective but astronomically applied
entries.status: unconditional (Corollary 1.3 rests on a rigorous computation)
entries.authors: Michael Griffin, Ken Ono, Larry Rolen, Jesse Thorner, Zachary Tripp, Ian Wagner
entries.technique: Low-lying zeros of the derivatives xi^{(n)}(s) control hyperbolicity of J^{d,n}; partial RH verification for xi^{(m)} to height T buys degree d <= floor(T)^2 wholesale.
entries.gap: Corollary 1.3 (arXiv v3, Dec 2020) still uses Platt's 3.06x10^10; inserting Platt-Trudgian's 3x10^12 (arXiv:2004.09765) immediately gives d <= 9x10^24, an unharvested free update. More substantively: RH_m(T) for m >= 1 (zeros of xi', xi'' verified to height T) has apparently never been rigorously computed, so the m >= 1 arm of Theorem 1.2 has never been fed.
entries.bottleneck: e^{d/2} growth in the unconditional threshold; the conditional route needs enclosure-checked zero verification for derivatives of xi, which nobody has produced.
entries.optimization_variables: verification height T per derivative order m; the exponent in d <= floor(T)^2 (is T^2 optimal?); effective constant c
entries.computational_tractability: Very high: rigor.py enclosure-checked sign changes plus argument-principle counts apply verbatim to Xi'(t).
entries.formalization_tractability: Theorem 1.2's deduction is finite case analysis over low-lying zeros; candidate for Lean.

entries.result: Farmer's critique: Jensen polynomials are not a plausible route to RH
entries.statement: The Hermite universality of GORZ is a 'new type of universal law' but carries no information about RH: hyperbolicity of J^{d,n} for fixed d and large n concerns only a bounded region of the critical strip, and the suggested connections to GUE statistics are unjustified. Farmer proposes criteria for when an RH-equivalence is useful (roughly: it must not become trivially true 'in the limit' for reasons disjoint from RH).
entries.authors: David W. Farmer
entries.technique: Analysis of what fixed-degree hyperbolicity actually constrains about zero locations; comparison with functions violating RH that satisfy the same asymptotic laws.
entries.bottleneck: Not a theorem but a decisive framing constraint: any Territory-G project claiming RH-relevance must survive the Farmer criteria and the Davenport-Heilbronn battery.
entries.gap: Farmer's criteria have not been systematically run against the newer bases (Romik's Meixner-Pollaczek / continuous Hahn expansions), where Romik conjectures more natural structure; whether those expansions also satisfy an RH-independent universal law is open and testable.
entries.computational_tractability: Lab's epstein.battery is precisely the falsification instrument Farmer's criteria call for.
entries.formalization_tractability: n/a (methodological)

entries.result: Unconditional Turan (d=2) and higher-order Turan (d=3) inequalities for xi
entries.statement: Write 8 xi(1/2 + sqrt(z))-style moment coefficients b_n (Csordas-Norfolk-Varga normalization). Csordas-Norfolk-Varga (1986): the Turan inequalities b_n^2 - b_{n-1} b_{n+1} >= 0 hold for all n >= 1 (equivalently J^{2,n} hyperbolic for all n). Dimitrov-Lucas (2011): the higher-order (cubic) Turan inequalities 4(b_n^2 - b_{n-1}b_{n+1})(b_{n+1}^2 - b_n b_{n+2}) - (b_n b_{n+1} - b_{n-1}b_{n+2})^2 >= 0 hold for all n >= 1, unconditionally (equivalently J^{3,n} hyperbolic for all n). These are the only two degrees with purely analytic (computation-free) proofs for all n.
entries.authors: George Csordas, Timothy Norfolk, Richard Varga (d=2); Dimitar Dimitrov, Fabio Lucas (d=3)
entries.citation: Trans. AMS 296 (1986) 521-541; Proc. AMS 139 (2011) 1013-1022, 'Higher order Turan inequalities for the Riemann xi-function'
entries.technique: Explicit integral inequalities for the moments of the kernel Phi(t) (log-concavity plus refined convexity estimates of Phi).
entries.bottleneck: The kernel-moment method has not been pushed past d=3; each degree requires a bespoke sharp inequality for Phi.
entries.gap: No analytic proof of J^{4,n} hyperbolicity for all n exists (only the computation-backed d <= 9.36x10^20 result). Whether the Dimitrov-Lucas approach extends to d=4 with modern computer-assisted inequality certification (SOS / interval methods on Phi's moment quotients) is open.
entries.optimization_variables: auxiliary kernel inequalities for Phi; SOS certificates for polynomial inequalities in the moment ratios
entries.verified_via: https://bv.fapesp.br/en/publicacao/29040/higher-order-turan-inequalities-for-the-riemann-xi-function (search-level confirmation of Dimitrov-Lucas statement); details memory-unverified
entries.computational_tractability: High: moments of Phi computable to arbitrary precision; enclosure-checked with Arb.
entries.formalization_tractability: d=2 (CNV) is a realistic Lean target: one explicit kernel inequality plus finite checking.

entries.result: Conrey 1983: proportions of zeros of xi^(m) on the critical line, and simple
entries.statement: Let alpha_m be the proportion of zeros of xi^{(m)}(s) with Re = 1/2, and beta_m the proportion on Re = 1/2 that are simple. Paper I: alpha_1 >= 0.8137 and alpha_m = 1 + O(m^{-2}) as m -> infinity. Paper II theorem: beta_m > 1 - log F_m(R) / R for any R > 0, with F_m built from phi(x) = 1 - x; Corollary 1: beta_0 > 0.3485, beta_1 > 0.7869, beta_2 > 0.9314, beta_3 > 0.9666, beta_4 > 0.9799, beta_5 > 0.9863, and beta_m = 1 + O(m^{-2}). Corollary 2: the proportion delta_m of zeta zeros of multiplicity > m satisfies delta_m < 1/m^2 (from the simple-zero counts).
entries.authors: J. Brian Conrey
entries.citation: J. Number Theory 16 (1983) 49-74 (I) and J. Number Theory 17 (1983) 71-75 (II)
entries.technique: Levinson's method applied to xi^{(m)} via a new identity expressing xi^{(m)}(1/2+it) through G_m(s); mollified mean values with the linear mollifier phi(x) = 1 - x and one free parameter R.
entries.bottleneck: The entire 40-year-old machinery uses Levinson's original mollifier phi(x) = 1-x and short mollifier length; none of the modern mollifier technology (Conrey 1989 theta=4/7, Bui-Conrey-Young, Pratt-Robles-Zaharescu-Zeindler multi-piece mollifiers, 2025 short-mollifier derivative combinations) has ever been transplanted back into the xi^{(m)} problem.
entries.gap: alpha_1 and all beta_m are almost certainly improvable by several points with a modern mollifier; the optimization is a well-posed quadratic-form problem the literature has left unharvested since 1983.
entries.optimization_variables: mollifier polynomial phi (coefficients), mollifier length theta, parameter R, linear combinations of derivatives in the detector
entries.verified_via: https://aimath.org/~kaur/publications/4.pdf (PDF fetched; theorem, corollaries and exact decimals extracted from the text streams)
entries.computational_tractability: The variational problem (optimize phi, R) is numerically solvable in the lab before any analytic work.
entries.formalization_tractability: Hard (mean-value theorems); the final optimization inequality could be enclosure-checked numerically.

entries.result: Campbell-O'Rourke-Renfrew: Cosine and Hermite universality under repeated differentiation
entries.statement: For a class of even entire functions, real on the real line, with only real zeros (containing the rescalings relevant to Xi under RH), the zeros of the n-th derivative, suitably rescaled, converge to an arithmetic progression (zeros of cosine) as n -> infinity: this proves the Cosine Universality conjecture of Farmer-Rhoades (2005). They also prove Hermite universality and finite-free-probability analogues of the LLN, CLT and Poisson limit theorem for deterministic polynomial sequences.
entries.status: unconditional for the stated class; application to Xi itself is RH-conditional (needs all-real zeros)
entries.authors: Andrew Campbell, Sean O'Rourke, David Renfrew
entries.technique: Finite free probability: repeated differentiation as finite free convolution powers; free-probabilistic limit theorems transferred to root distributions.
entries.bottleneck: The real-rootedness hypothesis: for Xi unconditionally one only knows a proportion >= 2/3 of zeros on the line, and the finite-free machinery has no version tolerating a sparse set of non-real zeros.
entries.gap: Unconditional cosine universality for Xi^{(n)} (using Ki-Kim-Lee-type 'finitely many non-real zeros after smoothing' or Conrey's alpha_m -> 1) is open; quantitative convergence rates (in n, at fixed height) are not established; behavior for the Davenport-Heilbronn function (real coefficients, off-line zeros) is untested.
entries.optimization_variables: rescaling windows; coupling between differentiation count n and height T
entries.computational_tractability: Very high: lab computes Xi and derivatives at arbitrary precision; spacing statistics machinery exists in statistics.py.
entries.formalization_tractability: Low near-term; finite free probability absent from Mathlib.

entries.result: Michalowski 2026: de Bruijn-Newman kernel is not a Polya frequency function of order 5
entries.statement: The kernel K(u) = Phi(|u|) (Phi the super-exponentially decaying heat kernel with H_0(z) = integral Phi(u) cos(zu) du) is not PF_5: at (u_0, h) = (0.01, 0.05) an explicit 5x5 Toeplitz minor has determinant rigorously enclosed in [-1.8472496e-9, -1.8472225e-9]. The minors D_2, D_3, D_4 are positive at that configuration; global PF_4 status is left open. Version 2 withdrew v1's asymptotic-threshold claims because of unsound derivative-tail enclosures; the central counterexample stands.
entries.authors: Wojciech Michalowski
entries.technique: 80-digit outward-rounded interval arithmetic with proved truncation bounds for theta series; independent cross-check via explicit Leibniz expansions of the minors.
entries.bottleneck: The withdrawn v1 asymptotics mean the field currently lacks any correct account of where PF_k fails as a function of (u_0, h, k); only one enclosure-checked point exists.
entries.gap: Global PF_4 status of K is explicitly open; the 'Toeplitz threshold phenomenon' (v1) is unproven; nobody has mapped the sign of D_4 and D_5 minors over the (u_0, h) plane with enclosure-checked arithmetic. This is a fresh (Feb 2026) surface with essentially one paper on it.
entries.optimization_variables: configuration (u_0, h), minor order k, node placement in the Toeplitz matrix, theta-series truncation depth
entries.computational_tractability: Extremely high for this lab: Phi, theta tails, and Arb enclosures are exactly zeta-lab's core machinery.
entries.formalization_tractability: A single enclosure-checked negative determinant is a bounded computation: near-ideal Lean interval-arithmetic target (compare lean/ rung-3 interval layers).

entries.result: Romik: orthogonal polynomial expansions of Xi
entries.statement: Expansions of Xi(t) in three bases: Hermite polynomials (Turan's program), symmetric Meixner-Pollaczek polynomials P_n^{(3/4)}(x; pi/2), and continuous Hahn polynomials p_n(x; 3/4, 3/4, 3/4, 3/4). In each basis the coefficients alternate in sign, and Romik proves asymptotic formulas for them, plus a new asymptotic formula for the Taylor coefficients of xi. He argues the Meixner-Pollaczek and Hahn expansions may be more natural than Hermite for approaching RH.
entries.authors: Dan Romik
entries.technique: Mellin/theta manipulations of the Phi kernel; classical orthogonal polynomial asymptotics; saddle point analysis.
entries.bottleneck: No hyperbolicity/Turan theory has been developed in the new bases: the analogue of the Jensen-Polya criterion for Meixner-Pollaczek or Hahn coefficient sequences is not even formulated precisely in the literature.
entries.gap: Whether Turan-type or higher-order inequalities hold for Romik's Meixner-Pollaczek/Hahn coefficients (and whether they are RH-discriminating, i.e. fail for Davenport-Heilbronn) is open and finitely testable.
entries.optimization_variables: choice of orthogonality parameters (the 3/4's), which coefficient functionals to test, degree/shift ranges
entries.computational_tractability: High: coefficients are explicit integrals against Phi, computable with mpmath/Arb.
entries.formalization_tractability: Moderate: alternating-sign proofs are contour-integral arguments.

entries.result: Platt-Trudgian: RH verified to height 3x10^12
entries.statement: All non-trivial zeros rho of zeta with 0 < Im rho <= 3x10^12 satisfy Re rho = 1/2; verified rigorously using interval arithmetic (12,363,153,437,138 zeros). This is the current rigorous input feeding both the conditional Lambda <= 0.20 and the Jensen degree bound d <= floor(3x10^12)^2 = 9x10^24.
entries.authors: Dave Platt, Tim Trudgian
entries.technique: Turing's method with enclosure-checked evaluation of Z(t) via interval arithmetic.
entries.bottleneck: Compute cost; and crucially no analogous rigorous verification exists for zeros of xi' or higher derivatives (RH_m(T), m >= 1).
entries.gap: RH_1(T) for any nontrivial T is absent from the literature; even T ~ 10^6 would be new and would activate the n >= 1 arm of GORTTW Theorem 1.2.
entries.optimization_variables: height T, derivative order m, verification algorithm (Turing method adapted to Xi^{(m)})
entries.computational_tractability: The m >= 1 analogue is directly buildable on rigor.py (enclose_Z, proven_sign, enclosure-checked_zero_count).
entries.formalization_tractability: Turing-method certification in Lean is a known hard but circumscribed problem.

entries.result: O'Sullivan: Hermite-combination criterion and sharp asymptotics for xi Taylor coefficients
entries.statement: A reformulation of Polya's Jensen-polynomial criterion for RH using linear combinations of Hermite polynomials, shown to hold 'in many cases'; plus detailed asymptotic expansions (to arbitrary order) for the Taylor coefficients of xi at 1/2 and related quantities, sharpening the asymptotics underlying Griffin-Ono-Rolen-Zagier.
entries.authors: Cormac O'Sullivan
entries.citation: arXiv:2007.13582; Research in the Mathematical Sciences 8 (2021)
entries.technique: Saddle-point asymptotic expansions of the theta-kernel moments; Hermite polynomial recombination of the Jensen criterion.
entries.bottleneck: Same d-uniformity wall as GORZ; the improved asymptotics have not been fed back into the effective threshold n >= c e^{d/2} to shrink c or the exponent.
entries.gap: Recomputing the GORTTW effective constant c using O'Sullivan's higher-order expansions is an unharvested improvement; nobody has checked how far the 'many cases' of the new criterion extend computationally.
entries.optimization_variables: order of asymptotic expansion; Hermite combination coefficients
entries.computational_tractability: High: expansions are explicit and checkable against lab's high-precision xi coefficients.
entries.formalization_tractability: Moderate.

entries.result: Heat-flow and finite-free differentiation dynamics (2024-2026 activity)
entries.statement: Active adjacent work: Hall-Ho 'heat flow conjecture' for polynomials and random matrices (Lett. Math. Phys. 115 (2025) 60); Hall-Ho-Jalowy-Kabluchko on roots under repeated differentiation and fractional differential operators (arXiv:2312.14883); 'The Rectangular Finite Free Heat Flow' (arXiv:2606.06859, June 2026); 'Zeros of polynomial powers under the heat flow' (arXiv:2512.17808, Dec 2025); Galligo-Najnudel-Vu on rotationally invariant root sets under iterated differentiation (arXiv:2506.06263, 2025). Collectively: heat flow and differentiation act as free convolution semigroups on root measures, with universal local limits.
entries.authors: Brian Hall, Ching-Wei Ho, Jonas Jalowy, Zakhar Kabluchko, Andre Galligo, Joseph Najnudel, Truong Vu, and others
entries.technique: Finite free probability, free convolution semigroups, PDE for log-potential of root measures.
entries.bottleneck: All results are for polynomials or random models; transfer to the single deterministic transcendental object Xi (order-1 entire, log-concave kernel) is not done, and the H_t flow on Xi zeros is exactly the t-parametrized version these papers study abstractly.
entries.gap: A dictionary between the Polymath15 effective H_t dynamics and the finite-free heat flow limit theorems has not been written; measured spacing statistics of H_t zeros for t in (0, 0.2] against the free-convolution prediction is an open numerical test.
entries.optimization_variables: flow time t, height window, rescaling; choice of free-probability observable (Cauchy transform vs spacings)
entries.verified_via: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17808 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.06859 (titles/abstract-level); Hall-Ho citation memory-unverified in detail
entries.computational_tractability: High: heatflow.py tracks H_t zeros directly.
entries.formalization_tractability: Low near-term.

candidate_projects.title: Rigorous RH_1(T): enclosure-checked verification that all zeros of xi' up to height T lie on the critical line
candidate_projects.description: Build on zeta/rigor.py to certify, via Arb ball arithmetic, that all zeros of xi'(s) with |Im s| <= T lie on Re s = 1/2 and are simple, for T ~ 10^6-10^9. Concretely: (a) count zeros of xi' in the rectangle by a enclosure-checked argument-principle integral of xi''/xi' on a box contour (xi' is entire, no pole issues); (b) count sign changes of the real function d/dt Xi(t) = derivative of Hardy-type Xi on the line with proven_sign; (c) equality of the two counts is exactly RH_1(T). No rigorous RH_1(T) computation exists in the literature at any height, and via GORTTW Theorem 1.2 (arXiv:1910.01227) any T immediately yields 'J^{d,n} hyperbolic for all n >= 1 and d <= floor(T)^2', a new unconditional theorem-grade finite statement. First signal (hours): enclosure-checked count agreement on T = 1000. Falsified cheaply if the argument-principle enclosures blow up near Gram-point-like degeneracies (visible in the first box).
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 1-2 days to a enclosure-checked count at T=10^3; ~2 weeks to T=10^6

candidate_projects.title: Modern mollifier transplant into Conrey's 1983 xi^(m) framework
candidate_projects.description: Conrey's beta_1 > 0.7869 (simple zeros of xi' on the line) and alpha_1 >= 0.8137 use Levinson's original mollifier phi(x) = 1-x and one free parameter R, untouched since 1983. Step 1 (numerical, this lab): re-derive Conrey's functional F_m(R) for general polynomial phi (his paper reduces to the same Q_m analysis with phi arbitrary), then optimize phi's coefficients and R as a finite-dimensional quadratic-form problem in mpmath; this mirrors the lab's prior gap-census transplant methodology. Step 2 (analytic): verify the mean-value theorem tolerates the optimized phi (it does for Levinson-Conrey classes) and longer theta via Conrey 1989 / PRZZ technology. First signal (days): the numerical optimum for beta_1 exceeds 0.80 with phi of degree <= 4; if optimization of phi gains < 0.005, the project dies cheaply. Distinct from the lab's prior critical-line-proportion project (different theorem, different functional).
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 3-5 days for the general-phi functional and first optimization
candidate_projects.key_reference: B. Conrey, J. Number Theory 17 (1983) 71-75 (verified via https://aimath.org/~kaur/publications/4.pdf)

candidate_projects.title: Global PF_4 status of the de Bruijn-Newman kernel: enclosure-checked minor atlas
candidate_projects.description: Michalowski (arXiv:2602.20313, Feb 2026) proved K(u) = Phi(|u|) is not PF_5 via one enclosure-checked negative 5x5 Toeplitz minor at (u_0,h) = (0.01,0.05), withdrew his v1 asymptotic-threshold claims as unsound, and left global PF_4 open. Project: reproduce his 5x5 enclosure with zeta-lab's Phi + Arb (independent check of a 6-month-old result), then run a enclosure-checked scan of 4x4 Toeplitz minors D_4(u_0,h) over a log-spaced grid u_0 in [10^-4, 10], h in [10^-4, 1]. Outcome A: a enclosure-checked negative D_4 kills PF_4 (a publishable finite theorem, one determinant). Outcome B: an all-positive atlas plus a correct proof of the tail asymptotics (fixing what v1 botched) establishes the threshold phenomenon. First signal (hours): reproduction of the [-1.8472496e-9, -1.8472225e-9] enclosure. Falsification: if D_4 is uniformly and robustly positive with margins growing at the grid edges, Outcome A is dead within a day and the project pivots to B or stops.
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: hours (reproduce the enclosure-checked 5x5 minor), 2-3 days for the D_4 atlas

candidate_projects.title: Harvest and extend: Jensen hyperbolicity degree bound 9.36x10^20 -> 9x10^24 and the Lean-checked corollary
candidate_projects.description: GORTTW Corollary 1.3 (arXiv v3) derives 'J^{d,n} hyperbolic for all n >= 0, d <= 9.36x10^20' from Platt's RH_0(3.06x10^10). Inserting Platt-Trudgian's rigorous RH_0(3x10^12) (arXiv:2004.09765) through Theorem 1.2 gives d <= 9.0000...x10^24 immediately. Two deliverables: (1) check the published Advances version has not already made this substitution (30 minutes; if it has, this arm dies and only arm 2 survives); (2) formalize the deduction 'RH_0(T) and d <= floor(T)^2 implies hyperbolicity for all n' style finite corollary in Lean 4, taking RH_0(T) as a named hypothesis, making it the first kernel-checked statement in the Jensen-Polya program. The Lean arm needs only polynomial real-rootedness plus the GORTTW combinatorial deduction, not zeta analytics. First signal: the published-version check plus a Lean skeleton with the deduction stated and one lemma closed.
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 30 minutes for the harvest check; 1-2 weeks for a meaningful Lean skeleton

candidate_projects.title: Cosine universality rates for Xi^(n) and the Davenport-Heilbronn discriminant test
candidate_projects.description: Campbell-O'Rourke-Renfrew (arXiv:2410.06403) prove Farmer-Rhoades cosine universality qualitatively for real-rooted even entire functions; no rates are known and Xi is covered only under RH. Numerical program: compute zeros of Xi^{(n)} for n = 1..64 in the window t in [0, 500] at high precision (derivatives via the Hermite/Turan expansion of Xi, whose coefficients Romik's asymptotics control), measure the deviation-from-equal-spacing statistic Delta(n) = normalized variance of consecutive gaps, and fit the decay rate (conjecture: Delta(n) ~ c/n, testable). Then run the identical pipeline on the Davenport-Heilbronn function (epstein.py): since DH violates RH but has real coefficients and a Hardy-type Z, whether differentiation equalizes its on-line spacing at the same rate is exactly Farmer's discriminance question, and either answer is a robust publishable conjecture with a battery-passing methodology. First signal (1-2 days): Delta(n) curve for n <= 16 for Xi; falsified as a project if derivative zero computation loses precision before any trend is visible.
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 1-2 days for the first Delta(n) decay curve

candidate_projects.title: Turan-type inequalities in Romik's Meixner-Pollaczek and continuous Hahn bases
candidate_projects.description: Romik (arXiv:1902.06330) proved his Meixner-Pollaczek and continuous Hahn expansion coefficients of Xi alternate in sign and suggested these bases are more natural than Hermite for RH, but no Jensen/Turan-type theory exists in them. Project: (a) compute the coefficient sequences c_n to 50+ digits (explicit integrals against Phi, Arb-certifiable); (b) test Turan and cubic Turan inequalities for |c_n| for n <= 5000; (c) run the identical computation for the Davenport-Heilbronn analogue (its kernel is a finite combination of Epstein theta data) to see whether any inequality that holds for Xi fails for DH: a discriminating inequality would be the first Farmer-criteria-passing positivity statement in this corner and a genuinely new conjecture; a non-discriminating one is a documented negative result. First signal (days): the n <= 500 table for both functions. Cheap falsification: DH satisfies everything Xi does (likely per docs/09 experience), settled within a week.
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 3-4 days for both coefficient tables and the first inequality census

candidate_projects.title: Rerun and re-optimize the Polymath15 barrier: publish Lambda <= 0.20 (or lower)
candidate_projects.description: The unconditional record is Lambda <= 0.22 (arXiv:1904.12438); the improvement to 0.20 enabled by Platt-Trudgian's 3x10^12 verification exists only as a Polymath-wiki remark and was never published or optimized. Project: port the public dbn_upper_bound pipeline (github.com/km-git-acc/dbn_upper_bound) onto the lab's Arb stack, reproduce the 0.22 certificate, then re-place the barrier at the 3x10^12 frontier and re-optimize (t_0, barrier x_0, mesh) to find the true minimum t the current verified height supports (plausibly below 0.20, since the wiki number was not optimized). Every step is a finite enclosure-checked computation; the deliverable is an unconditional record constant with a reproducible certificate, exactly this lab's genre. First signal (week 1): independent reproduction of the 0.22 barrier certificate. Cheap falsification: if reproduction cost is prohibitive at lab scale, stop; scaling estimates are visible after the first barrier run.
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: ~1 week to reproduce the 0.22 certificate, 2-4 weeks for a new constant

candidate_projects.title: Effective Ki-Kim-Lee: enclosure-checked non-real-zero-free heights for H_t at fixed t > 0
candidate_projects.description: Ki-Kim-Lee (Adv. Math. 222 (2009)) prove H_t has only finitely many non-real zeros for each t > 0 but give no effective bound. Polymath15's effective A+B approximation already controls H_t above explicit heights for t near 0.2. Project: for a ladder of fixed times t in {0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2}, produce enclosure-checked statements 'all zeros of H_t with |Im z| > 0 lie in |Re z| <= X(t), and H_t has exactly k(t) non-real zeros' by combining the Polymath15 effective bounds (above the barrier) with Arb contour counts (below it). This turns a qualitative 2009 theorem into the first quantitative non-real-zero census of the de Bruijn-Newman flow, directly reusable by anyone attacking Lambda from above, and the k(t) curve as t decreases toward Lambda is itself new measured structure (how the flow sheds complex zeros). First signal (days): a enclosure-checked count k(0.2) = 0 up to height 1000 reproducing barrier-region behavior; falsified if the A+B error terms are too weak below Polymath15's x-range to close any box.
candidate_projects.time_to_first_signal: 3-5 days for the first enclosure-checked box count at t=0.2
candidate_projects.key_reference: Ki-Kim-Lee, Adv. Math. 222 (2009) 281-306; arXiv:1904.12438 effective estimates
